# Psalm 145 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Song of Praise. Of David. I will extol you, my God and King, and bless your name forever and ever.

**2** Every day I will bless you and praise your name forever and ever.

**3** Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised, and his greatness is unsearchable.

**4** One generation shall commend your works to another, and shall declare your mighty acts.

**5** On the glorious splendor of your majesty, and on your wondrous works, I will meditate.

**6** They shall speak of the might of your awesome deeds, and I will declare your greatness.

**7** They shall pour forth the fame of your abundant goodness and shall sing aloud of your righteousness.

**8** The LORD is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.

**9** The LORD is good to all, and his mercy is over all that he has made.

**10** All your works shall give thanks to you, O LORD, and all your saints shall bless you!

**11** They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom and tell of your power,

**12** to make known to the children of man your mighty deeds, and the glorious splendor of your kingdom.

**13** Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and your dominion endures throughout all generations.

**14** The LORD upholds all who are falling and raises up all who are bowed down.

**15** The eyes of all look to you, and you give them their food in due season.

**16** You open your hand; you satisfy the desire of every living thing.

**17** The LORD is righteous in all his ways and kind in all his works.

**18** The LORD is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

**19** He fulfills the desire of those who fear him; he also hears their cry and saves them.

**20** The LORD preserves all who love him, but all the wicked he will destroy.

**21** My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 145.

- **145:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **145:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **145:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **145:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **145:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **145:12** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **145:1-21**: The last Davidic psalm and the only psalm titled tehillah ('praise'). An acrostic (aleph-tav, minus nun in MT — supplied in DSS and LXX).
- **145:8-9**: Exodus 34:6 quoted again — 'gracious and-compassionate... slow-of-anger' — with the universalizing addition: 'Good to-all... his-compassion over-all his-works.'
- **145:16**: 'Opening your-hand, and-satisfying to-every living-thing desire' — divine generosity extending to all creation, not just Israel.

### LOGOS
- **145:8-9**: This psalm extends the Exodus 34:6 formula to universal scope: God is not just compassionate to Israel but 'good to all' and merciful 'over all that he has made.' This is the broadest statement of divine benevolence in the Psalter.
- **145:13**: 'Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom' — the psalm that begins with David the king praising God as King culminates in the permanence of divine rule over all temporal kingdoms.

### PNEUMA
- **145:8-9**: God is good to EVERYONE. His compassion covers EVERYTHING he's made. These two verses are the Psalms' most expansive statement of God's love — not limited by nationality, religion, or species.
- **145:14-16**: God catches the falling, lifts the burdened, feeds every living creature. This isn't theology in the abstract — it's God showing up in the most practical ways possible.

— SOPHIA
